findings.title: Reader thread is never joined before asserting on caughtExceptions, making the test racy and leaky
findings.body: In createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, after deletedAll.set(true) the test immediately asserts assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty()) without joining the reader thread. The reader thread may still be in the middle of a groups() request when deletedAll flips, so an NPE thrown by that in-flight request is added to caughtExceptions after the assertion has already passed — the very race this test is meant to catch can be missed, and the test can pass while the bug still reproduces. Additionally the raw thread is never joined or interrupted, so it keeps making admin requests after the test method (and possibly the class' realm) is torn down, which can cause flaky failures in later tests. The thread should be joined before asserting.

findings.title: Concurrent-deletion NPE remains in the paginated getSubGroupsStream variants
findings.body: The PR fixes the NPE in getSubGroupsCount by null-checking modelSupplier.get(), but the same race exists in the three adjacent methods: getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) at line 256, getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer) at line 262, and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) at line 268 all dereference modelSupplier.get() directly. modelSupplier is a LazyModel over getGroupModel(), which returns null when the group has been deleted concurrently (exactly the scenario of issue #40368). When that happens these methods still throw a NullPointerException, so the fix is incomplete for concurrent group deletion.

findings.title: getSubGroupsCount now silently returns null on concurrent deletion instead of failing fast
findings.body: With this change, getSubGroupsCount returns null when the underlying group has been concurrently deleted. Every other accessor in GroupAdapter that encounters a missing delegate either falls back to cached data or throws IllegalStateException("Not found in database") (see getDelegateForUpdate/isUpdated), while getRoleMappingsStream/getSubGroupsStream detect staleness and delegate to the DB. Returning a null Long here is inconsistent and will surface as a silently missing subGroupCount in GroupRepresentation (populated via GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount), which callers may not distinguish from a genuinely unknown count, and could NPE any code that auto-unboxes the result. Consider aligning the behavior with the rest of the adapter (throw or delegate) rather than returning null.
